title: Introduce heterogeneous batch splitter and hardware trace condenser
author: Maya Chen
description: Adds a new benchmark-lab workload component and a compact telemetry exporter. Motivation: current runners assume homogeneous GPU fleets and produce verbose kernel traces that are costly to store and slow to process. This PR introduces a deterministic heterogeneous batch splitter that simulates mixed-device routing and micro-batching across GPU/CPU backends with tunable skew and locality knobs, plus a hardware trace condenser that compacts per-kernel telemetry (timestamps, stream ids, kernel ids, memory ops) into a schema-stable CSV for flamegraph and ML attribution pipelines. Includes config-driven scenario definitions, seeded hashing for reproducibility, lossy and lossless condenser modes with sampling hooks, integration tests, CI job, compatibility shim for existing parsers, and docs. Checklist: implement splitter and condenser; add configs and CI; add integration perf tests; document loss/precision tradeoffs; collect cluster artifacts. Related work: ENG-1823, ENG-2037. No benchdriver API breaks.
